analysis:
Reviewed the visible changes: CHANGELOG.md excerpts (head lines 1031-1761) and the docs/developer/test.md patch at hunk @@ -2011. Both are documentation only. I found no executable code, auth, attestation, encryption, billing or routing changes in the supplied units.

The changelog entries describe the SSD prefix-cache work (T-041, TB-007) as unreleased: encrypted default SSD checkpoints, a 100 GiB ceiling limited to half of available space, and cache-scope revocation. The changelog's 100 GiB ceiling conflicts with the threat model's "no fixed ceiling" wording. That is documentation drift and not an exploitable regression. It is worth checking when the underlying code is reviewed. Those code changes (KVCacheSSD, SSDPrefixCachePolicy, the coordinator cache_route_keys scope derivation) are not in this batch, so their security properties are not verified here. This is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety.

The test.md patch adds a native lifecycle drain test command (testGracefulDrainAfterServedRequestRetiresNativeOwnerWithinDeadline). It has no security impact.

Unit 67373c0eff1153bd:0 is metadata only (the file's mode is unchanged) and has no content to examine. The next pass should check the actual SSD cache, allocator and telemetry code for T-041 and A-001 regressions, including TTL, disk budget, HMAC lookup naming and account scoping. It should also check whether the threat model needs updating if the 100 GiB ceiling and default-on behaviour are real.
